clue.text: Endeavour to catch a troublesome insect in cloth

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so the word for endeavour goes round the insect

parts.note: to endeavour is to try
a troublesome insect is a pest

explanation.surface: Someone tries to trap a bothersome bug lurking in some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed text lacks the 'a' needed: TRY 'catches' A PEST to give T-APEST-RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven wall-hanging, a kind of decorative fabric.

clue.text: It is getting comeuppance more than once from an Old Master

indicators.note: repeated more than once, so the turned word appears twice
in a down clue 'comeuppance' is read as 'come up', so the word It is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone keeps receiving their just deserts from a famous painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting comeuppance' turns IT into TI (it comes up the column); 'more than once' doubles it to TITI, and 'an' is spelt out to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was a great Venetian Renaissance painter, a classic Old Master.

clue.text: Digest of revised prices

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters of prices are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A summary of a new price list.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a summary, and a precis is a short summary of a text.

clue.text: Scholars go up to city for a day

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates or scholars
Bath is a city in Somerset, England

explanation.surface: Academics travel up to town for a day out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go up' turns BAS into SAB; Bath is an English spa city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day of rest and worship.

clue.text: Turn-over at the bakery

parts.note: a baker's product that is ... up, read cryptically as something turned over

explanation.definitionFit: A roll is a small bread loaf, and to roll is to turn over.

clue.text: Slight injury to King in country

indicators.note: the King's letter is placed inside the country's name

parts.note: Spain is a European country
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch picks up a minor knock while abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is a wrenched joint or ligament, a minor injury.

clue.text: Panther running wild in Wales

definitions.note: the definition points to a place found in Wales

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so the letters of Panther are scrambled

explanation.surface: A big cat on the loose in the Welsh countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running wild' rearranges PANTHER. PENARTH is a seaside town near Cardiff in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Penarth is a coastal town in south Wales, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: A metal container so suitable for the plant

parts.note: a can is a metal container
so means thus, therefore

explanation.surface: A tin can therefore makes a good pot for the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a Mediterranean plant with spiny leaves, copied in classical architecture.

clue.text: Such people have no right to seed

parts.note: taken as written
semen is seed in the sense of sperm

explanation.surface: A remark about people lacking any claim to plant seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such people' points back to the wordplay; the Norsemen were the Vikings.
explanation.definitionFit: Norsemen were the medieval Scandinavians, a people famous as Viking raiders.

clue.text: That particularly round, hairless man

parts.note: the stressed 'the' means that particular one
O is round in shape
hairless means bald

explanation.surface: Describing a specific round-headed, bald chap.
explanation.walkthrough: THE said with stress (thee) singles out one particular thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Theobald is a man's given name, so it stands for a male person.

clue.text: Putting an international organisation on the market is not ethical

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations
a fair is a market or trade show

explanation.surface: Selling off a global body would be morally wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair means unjust, so lacking in moral rightness.

clue.text: Beetle seen to move swiftly under sack

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: to sack is to fire from a job
to fly is to move swiftly

explanation.surface: An insect dashes away beneath a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts FLY below FIRE in the column. Fireflies are in fact beetles.
explanation.definitionFit: Fireflies are luminous nocturnal beetles of the family Lampyridae.

clue.text: This creature goes back to get one blade of grass

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a lamina is a thin layer or the blade of a leaf

explanation.surface: A grazing beast returns for a single blade of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes back' turns LAMINA, the botanical term for a leaf blade, around.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is a living creature, a beast.

clue.text: Tiger ate dicky-just a few feathers to be seen

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, so the letters of Tiger ate are disordered

explanation.surface: A tiger has eaten a dodgy bird and only some feathers remain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dicky' (British slang for unreliable) rearranges TIGER ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aigrette is a small tuft of plumes, such as an egret's head plumes.

clue.text: Two eggs inside this incubator

parts.note: the word contains two O letters, eggs in shape, and describes a heated box for a brood

explanation.definitionFit: A brooder is a heated enclosure for raising chicks.

clue.text: Hire lodge for the school

parts.note: to charter is to hire a vessel or vehicle
to lodge is to house someone

explanation.surface: Renting a cottage for a school group.
explanation.walkthrough: Charterhouse is a famous English private school in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Charterhouse is a well-known English public school in Godalming.

clue.text: Disciplines in harshest possible way

indicators.note: in some possible way means arranged otherwise, so the letters of harshest are reordered

explanation.surface: Punishes someone as severely as can be.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash is to beat as punishment, so it means punishes.

clue.text: Man's work, converting far attic

indicators.note: converting means changing, so the letters of far attic are reworked

explanation.surface: A craftsman's job turning a distant loft into a room.
explanation.definitionFit: An artifact is an object made by human hands.

clue.text: Tough joint lying beside the motorway

definitions.note: the definition describes a strip of road found next to the main lanes

parts.note: tough means hard
the shoulder is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A stiff joint on someone lounging by the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: The hard shoulder is the British emergency lane along a motorway's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard shoulder is the paved emergency strip running alongside a British motorway.

clue.text: The model is about right for height

indicators.note: the model's word goes about, round, the letter for right

parts.note: a statue is a model of a figure

explanation.surface: A fashion model is nearly tall enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature is a person's natural standing size.

clue.text: Grain-holder subsequently made of clay

parts.note: an ear of corn holds the grain
subsequently means then, afterwards

explanation.surface: A grain store was later built from clay.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen means formed of baked earth, as earthenware pots are.

clue.text: Unfavourably reviewed what folk have done to get gold

definitions.meaning: critics who slate a show have savaged it

definitions.text: what folk have done to get gold
definitions.meaning: prospectors wash river gravel in a shallow dish to find gold

explanation.definitionFit: To pan is both to slate critically and to wash gravel for gold.

clue.text: Not even self-conscious about such poor workmanship

definitions.note: an adjective describing the clue's poor work

indicators.note: the word for self-conscious goes round the one for not even

parts.note: shy means self-conscious
odd numbers are not even

explanation.surface: A bashful craftsman ashamed of his uneven, badly made goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not even' is a straight synonym, not an instruction to take alternate letters; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy means badly made, of inferior quality.

clue.text: Full of enthusiasm I take a partner and set out

indicators.note: set out means arranged, so these letters are laid out anew

parts.note: to mate is to pair up with a partner

explanation.surface: Excited, I pair up with someone and head off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges I, MATE and AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated means lively and spirited.

clue.text: To draw it one must be quick

definitions.text: To draw it one must be quick

parts.words: To draw it one must be quick
parts.note: quick in its old sense of alive: only the living draw air into their lungs

explanation.definitionFit: Breath is air drawn into the lungs, something only the living can take.

clue.text: Type of magpie

definitions.meaning: a size of printing type, twelve points
The scientific genus name of the magpie

explanation.definitionFit: Pica is both a printer's type size and the Latin genus of the magpie.

clue.text: Embarrassed, I shut a revealing gap

indicators.note: embarrassed means flustered or thrown, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Red-faced, I close a gap that was showing too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embarrassed' rearranges I and SHUT A; the printed text lacks the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a break or interruption in continuity.

clue.text: Forced to withdraw the second I rang

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
rang means telephoned

explanation.surface: Someone made to pull out the moment they called.
explanation.definitionFit: Siphoned means drawn off through a tube by pressure, liquid forced out of a vessel.

clue.text: Planter's dog

definitions.meaning: one who sets or plants things in place
a gundog breed, such as the Irish red

explanation.definitionFit: A setter is both one who sets plants and a gundog breed.

clue.text: Duck's delight-save for this

definitions.meaning: the idiom of putting money by for hard times

explanation.definitionFit: Ducks enjoy wet weather, and people save money for a time of need.
